utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has protective measures, but he signed the document, so we must put this exhibit under seal. Can we have an IC number under seal, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document just signed by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC01124, under seal. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 1024 or 1124? 11, okay. [Interpretation] That's the right number now. It's been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, let's leave the map for a moment and look at document 4D626. Document 4D426 -- 626. 626. It's a map showing the general area of Konjic, similar to the one we were looking at a moment ago. The map was drawn by General Petkovic. We've already looked at it in this courtroom. The blue indicates places taken by the BH Army until the 24th of April, 1993, and the red indicates places which up until that time, including that date, the BH Army was still launching attacks on. Tell us, Witness, in the proofing sessions for today's testimony, did you analyse this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you have any suggestions to make? Are there any locations which fell into BH Army hands that have not been marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, which those locations are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are Donje Selo, Galjevo - Galjevo is marked - Repovica, Pokojiste, Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And tell us, please, with that addition of yours, does this map correctly reflect the situation in this part of Konjic municipality at the end of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you now draw circles 'round the locations you've just mentioned; that is to say, Donje Selo, Pokojiste, Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Have you done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have to say I don't see what you've circled here, and could you do it on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donje Selo, Pokojiste, Celebici [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid we can't see it on our screens. Witness, can you see something on your screen when you're drawing on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counsel, just a second. The usher is coming to rectify the issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: In the meantime, to use the time, Witness, against whom was the ABiH fighting in these localities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The BH Army in these localities was fighting against the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, with that new pen, you can mark in those places.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donje Selo [marks], Pokojiste [marks], Celebici [marks], Repovica [marks], Kanjina [marks] and Podorasac [marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, do you agree that the witness not sign this document so we do not have to have it under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an IC number, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the aspect of the document just marked by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC01125. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I suggest that the witness puts "AB," his pseudonym, on the document, so this is better than nothing and doesn't have the danger of a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please place "4D-AB" on the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I am discovering this map drawn by General Petkovic. This is the situation on April 24, 1993. I am not versed in the military art like you are or like General Petkovic is, but any reasonable trier of fact could infer from this map that the HVO's military situation was becoming critical, insofar that a number of localities had been captured by the ABiH, that others were about to fall. Konjic was an enclave or pocket, so in military terms one could think that the next objective of this offensive was going to be Jablanica. As far as you know, at the end of April 1993 was the military situation of the HVO critical or becoming critical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, it did become critical, because until the end of that particular month all these places fell and had been taken control of by the BH Army. There was just one -- no, Konjic wasn't under siege. Konjic was under BH Army control. It was just an enclave around Zaselje and so on, that we were there, so that enclave remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So after drawing up this military panorama, couldn't you think that the next military target was going to be Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're going to try and demonstrate that to you in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, we have dealt with that map. Now look at the next document following on from that map. It is 4D140. It's a list of villages in Konjic municipality, and it was compiled in the Office for Refugees of the HZ-HB, Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons. Is that list correct, villages which fell into the hands of the BH Army and from which the Croatian population moved out? Whether they were displaced, forced out, or whatever, that's not important now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the list is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's go back to the IC number, IC1124. I think you still have it on your screen, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. A follow-up question, Witness. I have just now seen the list of these villages, these 23 villages, and my eye was immediately drawn to "Trusina." I remember very early on General Praljak wanted to present documents on massacres that had occurred in Trusina. Could you tell us how far Trusina is from Konjic in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Trusina is a distance of about 20 kilometres from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, did you receive any information according to which there had been murders against the Croatian inhabitants in a Croatian village, notably in Trusina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the very beginning of the conflict between the BH Army and Croatian Defence Council, our communication lines were poor because the BH Army interrupted our communications, so we didn't have information coming in about what was happening in other areas, nor in Trusina. We only learnt about that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that you learned about it later. How many months later, how many years later, or days later? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was two months afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you heard that massacres had occurred in a number of Croatian villages, at the Konjic municipality, a municipality which was not included in the indictment, could you tell us what happened, psychologically, in Konjic? You know, the people, inhabitants of Konjic, learning just a few months later that some of his [as interpreted] fellow Croats had been murdered, what do you feel about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to correct you. The inhabitants of Konjic municipality and Konjic, as a town, was also in the hands of the BH Army. I, myself, was in the enclave, the small pocket that was called Drecelj-Zabrdje-Zaslivlje-Turija, and it was in those places that we didn't have information. The telephones were down, the communications system was down, and we had daily fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're saying that the population in Konjic was already held by the ABiH, and in your enclave, all lines of communication were down and you had no idea what happened outside your enclave. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to correct the transcript in line 16, the enclave that the witness was talking about was the enclave that he defined as Drecelj, Zabrdje, Zaslivlje, and Turija. Zaslivlje, Turija. Turija. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Judge Antonetti asked you to explain, but there's no dilemma. When you said that it was only two months later that you learned about Trusina, do you mean you and the people who were in the enclave with you, or did you mean Croatians in general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just meant myself and the people who were in the enclave with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now bring up IC1124, the document we were looking at earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It is the map, Witness, that you marked with "5" and "7." Now, Witness, if we recall what the situation was like on the 24th of April, 1993, I'd like to ask you now, using this map, moving from right to left, to show us what territory the BH Army had taken control of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had taken control of this territory here [indicates], and I've already explained that, from Konjic towards the Neretvica River Valley. On the 24th, during that period, there was a small enclave, Vrce, which was not in the hands of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the following question, up until that date, the 24th of April, was the conclusion realised to a large extent that we saw under item 7 of this document, 4D454, the minutes from the meeting held on the 20th of March, what would you say? Was that implemented or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, almost entirely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's go back to document 4D454 so that we can analyse it fully. Do you have it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, under item 8, it says that an HVO unit should be relocated in, the Nihad Kulenovic unit. Tell us, please, Witness, where was that unit supposed -- where was it to be relocated, where from and where to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the village of Ovcari, and they asked that it be relocated to Ljubina. Now, in that HVO unit -- in the Croatian Defence Council unit that was called Nihad Kulenovic, you had members of the Muslim -- or, rather, you had Muslims in the unit with only three Croats. Darko Pandza [phoen] as commander of the unit, then there was Milan and Bacva [phoen], two Croats from Citluk or, rather, Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness, Ljubina, is that a hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a strategic elevation above Konjic separating the defence lines towards the Serbs and the Yugoslav People's Army, and it was a key feature in this general area, the most important elevation in that small enclave of ours which managed to resist the BH Army, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us slowly. Which enclave was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was this enclave here that I mentioned: Drecelj, Zabrdje, Zaslivlje, Turija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness, the BH Army, did it manage to relocate this HVO unit to Ljubina according to plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The BH Army was not successful in doing that, and the reason was that the company commander at that time who held that position did not agree to that relocation because -- if you want me to clarify, I can go on -- because within the composition of this unit, the Nihad Kulenovic unit, most of the members were Muslims. As for Ljubina, we already held that following an agreement with the -- well, the Muslims and the HVO or Croats held that, so had we exchanged our HVO Croat members at that particular locality and brought in members of the HVO who were Muslims, we would have -- or, rather, the enclave could not have survived because we would have been under a total siege and wouldn't have had control of that important elevation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please -- Witness, this document is dated the 20th of March, 1993. At that point in time, in the HVO units, were there Muslim soldiers who had joined you during 1992? Were they still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 24th, in our HVO units, there was not one Muslim, except for the Nihad Kulenovic unit, because on the 23rd of March, that is, one month earlier, all HVO members of Muslim ethnicity had left the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly to say that three days earlier, on the 23rd of March, when this document was drafted, the Muslims were still in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm sorry, I made a mistake. I leapt forward to April.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at Conclusion number 9. It says: "Prepare the ABiH units to take the Zlatar facility as soon as possible." Is that the telecom centre above ARK hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is that telecom centre that was located above ARK, and that is the most important telecommunications facility by means of which it was possible to set up communications in all the former Yugoslavia. It was dug into a mountain, it had seven underground storeys, and it was under complete protection, just like the ARK which was beneath it. And without the Zlatar facility, the ARK facility would have practically been cut off from the outside world, even including Sarajevo, so it would have been left without any function.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at Conclusion number 13. It says: "The elaboration of a plan of unitary operations for all forces in these areas is to be started immediately ..." How do you read this order, and how would you have interpreted it as a member of VOS if you had received it at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Attack plans are to be worked out urgently for the sectors in which the units were active that were familiar with this plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at Conclusion number 15. The Drecelj check-point is mentioned here. You said it was the only check-point controlled jointly by Croats and Muslims. It was to be dismantled by the 25th of March. If this conclusion had been implemented, what would that have meant with regard to the presence of Croats at that check-point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If this had been implemented, the Croats would have been removed from this check-point by which the M-17 road would have been under total control, so that there would have been no single Croat member of HVO along that communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. We're done with this document. Let us see what happened on the same day in the vicinity. Document 4D450.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one last question on this document. When reading this lengthy document, it looks like there is a specific plan, a very detailed plan, but my attention was drawn to item number 16. Under item 16, the following people are to be informed of these conclusions, and I discover that Mr. Izetbegovic is to be informed, even though he's in New York. He might have other things in mind in New York, but it seems he wants to be kept abreast of the way the plan is going. So what do you think of this? Mr. Izetbegovic is in New York, but wants to be informed of everything going on, notably what happens at the Drecelj post. What conclusion can you drawn from this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand your question fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat. When reading this lengthy document, this very detailed document which gives information on all the operations underway, I note that at item 16 there is a list of the people who are to be informed of these conclusions, a number of eminent people; the Wartime Presidency, the Supreme Command, the Ministry of Interior, the 4th Corps Command, and the Wartime Presidency in Jablanica, Konjic and Hadzici. But Mr. Izetbegovic must also be informed, even though he is in New York. It is written on this document, and my question is the following: Could you tell us why Mr. Izetbegovic wants to follow the implementation of this plan? Why is he supposed to be kept abreast of all these developments, even the small post in Drecelj? I mean, he is in New York. He probably has other things to do than checking on what's happening in Drecelj. What does this all mean, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can explain. When this document was drafted, the small enclave of Drecelj was not yet in existence. This was a plan for the action of the liberation of the Neretva Valley to be launched. Drecelj was not yet in existence. So I think that the president was to be informed of the entire plan and not only about the item mentioning Drecelj. Drecelj is not important here if the plan is carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that President Izetbegovic had to be informed of the plan, this plan that had to do with the Neretva Valley. But according to you, why is it that Mr. Izetbegovic, who is in New York, must be kept abreast of the advancement of the plan, of the progress of the plan? Maybe you don't know. Just tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, Mr. Izetbegovic had to be kept abreast because he was one of the people who knew of that plan, and they wanted to inform him of their activities in the Neretva Valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he is in New York. Why does he have to be informed all the way in New York? Wouldn't it be enough just to inform the Presidency in Sarajevo? Why is it that he must be informed, personally? Is there a meaning, militarily or politically or diplomatically? I don't know if you are competent to answer, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, probably it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that you cannot answer. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us now look at two documents to see what's happening with Mr. Cibo on the 20th of March, 1993, that is, on the same day when these conclusions were adopted. The first document is 4D450, 450. It's a decision of the Regional Committee of the SDA for Herzegovina for Safet Cibo to be co-opted into the Regional Committee of the party. Did you know, Witness, that Dr. Cibo was member of a highly positioned body in the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Look at the following document, 1D2756, 2756. This is an order issued by Sefer Halilovic by which Safet Cibo is assigned to the 4th Corps of the ABiH. Tell me, Witness, did you know that Dr. Cibo had a position in military structures, too, the structures of Muslim authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to object because of the leading questions. Ms. Alaburic is posing a lot of leading questions to this witness, and she should not put these questions into a leading form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are not leading questions. I was merely asking the witness whether he knows or doesn't know something. And the document is an exhibit anyway, so I'm not showing it to tender it; I'm merely asking the question whether he was aware of the fact or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Objection overruled. The objection is overruled. You're right, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We are now approaching the moment of the first conflict, the 23rd of March, 1993. Witness, please look at document 4D438. It's a report of the ABiH from Konjic which says: "We inform you that the situation in our area of responsibility is the following: 150 members of the HVO captured, town blocked, life in town paralysed. We continue with arrests." Signed: "Midhat Cerovac." Witness, did you know Mr. Cerovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is this an accurate description of the situation at Konjic on the 23rd of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document, 4D125. So it's a joint order of the chief of the HVO Main Staff and the commander of the 4th Corps of the ABiH, dated the 23rd of March, 1993, the order to the effect of disengaging. Did you know about this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Witness, what was the weather like at the time in the area of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 23rd of March, it wasn't really sunny, but it wasn't that cloudy either. But on the 24th of March, there was a snowfall in the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how much snow fell that evening or that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 30 centimetres of snow.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now look what happened until the end of the month. Document 4D806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, document 4D125 is really puzzling me. When I see all the documents from the 4th Corps that we have perused through, obviously there was an operation in the Neretva Valley underway. And on March 24, unless I'm wrong, General Petkovic and General Pasalic write a joint order calling for an immediate stop of everything. They want the release of all persons arrested, et cetera. So there I'm totally flabbergasted. I don't understand. So either there's a BH Army offensive underway, but then why would Pasalic ask for this operation to be halted, or there's an HVO offensive underway in the framework of an HVO plan, but then why would the operation be stopped? How is it that the two chiefs of these two armies agree on stopping everything? Could you give us a military explanation of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say the following: This is a document dated the 23rd of March, 1993, and the one before about the aggression was from April. And on the 23rd of March, 1993, the ABiH tried, with this action -- or, rather, tried to launch this action, which they finally did in April. So on the 23rd of March, in the morning, the whole town was blocked. All roads were blocked by the ABiH. Cars -- it was impossible to drive cars. It was only possible to pass on foot. At the check-point set up by the ABiH, members of the HVO were disarmed. Individuals were detained, and others were let go without weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I was putting this question to you because I did see the previous document, 4D438, dating March 23rd, and here we discover that 150 HVO soldiers were captured, that the city of Konjic is blocked, that the life in town is paralysed, and that "we continue with arrests." That's what the last bullet says. So obviously important things are happening, but on the very same day Pasalic, together with General Petkovic, makes an order that goes against all this. So is it because that there's sort of a double dealing with the international community going on, we solve matters covertly, and openly we try to pretend that we want a cease-fire and that we want peace, and we order cease-fires? Or is it because within the ABiH, itself, or within the HVO, itself, some people were carrying on different policies, which may explain why we have such a contradiction between document 4D38 [as interpreted] and 4D125? I'm trying to see the rationale behind all this, because we have an all-out attack, on one hand, and then, on the other hand, the person who supposedly should be in charge of this attack is signing a truce with General Petkovic. What do you make of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain it like this: Mr. Pasalic had his headquarters in Mostar, and at Konjic, it was the brigades that were ordered to do so, namely, the 7th Suad Alic Brigade, the Neretvica Brigade, and the newly arrived brigades in Konjic municipality carried out that task, which means that on the 23rd of March they disarmed about 150 soldiers, which means that the action agreed upon on the 20th of March and was signed and stamped with eight stamps, that its implementation began on the 23rd; that is, three days later. We insisted and requested our superiors that something be done because we were taken by surprise. On the 23rd, in the early-morning hours, our premises, the premises of the 2nd Battalion, were also blocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But you're not answering my question. Maybe you can't. But I'm very surprised because, on the one hand, the BiH Army is launching an offensive, captures the city of Konjic, but, on the other hand, Mr. Pasalic, an eminent member of the BH Army, signs a document according to which all this operation should be stopped. I don't understand, but maybe you cannot understand either because it's not in your field of competence. We'll see, anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I? Well, I can say that we insisted on negotiations and solving the problem through peaceful means, which probably General Milivoj Petkovic, our superior officer, tried to do with Mr. Pasalic. Now, how sincere Mr. Pasalic's intentions were, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, your questions are quite understandable and logical, and I hope that we will be able to provide answers to them by the end of this examination, but just let's get through the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, let's look at this 23rd of March. The conflict, in fact, was stopped straight away; is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me, Ms. Alaburic. I think we should be very clear about this. What we have here is an order, we have seen an order, so the question would be: Was this order implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This order was implemented, in part, but not on that same day, the 23rd of March. It was implemented several days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just observe that, since all these dates are critical, that on 4D125, before we leave it, now for some reason the date has got completely missed off the translation. It's very clear on the Croatian original, the one 23rd of March. It's just not there at all in the English. I just note that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, can you be a bit more precise and say what parts were implemented and which were not implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All parts of this order were implemented. And a cease-fire was implemented, but not on that day; several days -- three or four days after this order of the 23rd of March was passed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: How about the release of detained persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When a complete truce was put in place, then the commission started their work, and it was their task to release prisoners and to return the materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness, who did the HVO have in detention at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, the HVO had in detention a part of the Muderiz unit, as it was called.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at a few more documents on the topic we've just discussed. 4D806 is the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Ms. Alaburic. Witness, under item 6 of this order, it is said: "Understood that the possibility of aiding Tuzla, Usora and Sarajevo is dependent on your relations." I can understand as far as Sarajevo is concerned, but what about Tuzla and Usora? What was the problem in Tuzla and in Usora, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what problems they had in Tuzla and Usora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, as I said, the next document I'd like to deal with is 4D806, which is a permission and an order from the chief of the Main HVO Staff, and a joint commission of the BH and the HVO is mentioned which was sent to Konjic with the aim of calming the situation down where there were tensions. Tell us, Witness, did you know about the formation of this joint commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's take a look at the next document, which is 4D1556. 4D1556 is the number. This is a report from Arif Pasalic, sent to his superior, Sefer Halilovic, in which he informs him about the establishment of a commission which was to go to Jablanica and Konjic. And in point 2, it states the names of the members of that commission who were to contribute to the normalisation of relations. Tell us, Witness, did you know of the existence of this commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the arrival of this commission in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there when the commission came to Konjic because I was up at my positions at that time; that is to say, I was in Zlatar, the facility that I mentioned earlier on. However, I did take part in another commission that worked to calm the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the commission you worked in, did it have any authorisations with respect to filling in the trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did have that kind of authorisation, but what was more important was the exchange of prisoners and the return of MTS, which the BH Army refused to do. It refused to return the materiel and technical equipment, and weapons, in fact, which it had seized from members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document, 4D1558, once again an order from Arif Pasalic of that same day, the 23rd of March, 1993. And he is issuing this order to his units and commanders, telling them that they should establish contact with the Command of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade straight away and to release all prisoners on both sides. Tell us, please, Witness, this Herceg Stjepan Brigade, did it have anything to do with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. I was a member of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And at the time, did you reach an agreement with the BH Army to release all the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had negotiations like that for the release of all prisoners who were in detention at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's look at a different type of document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're going to have a break. It's 20 to 6.00. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's look at P1712, the next document, to see what the neighbouring brigade in Prozor was doing, the HVO, how they saw the situation in Konjic. Now, this is a report from Petar Kolakusic from the Rama Brigade in Prozor of the 23rd of March, 1993, and he says that: "Dramatic news is coming in from Konjic about the situation in the town," reporting that there're wounded and captured on both sides. "They request from the Rama Brigade artillery to open fire at the villages of Kruscica, Studencica and Jasenik." "We are asking for further instructions." Now, my question to you, Witness, is this: Was the situation in -- has the situation in Konjic been described properly? Was it that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, you from Konjic, did you ask for artillery support from the Rama Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you receive that artillery support?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's try and see the reasons for that now. Staying with that same piece of paper, we have the response from the commander of the operations zone, Zeljko Siljeg, who says: "Do not open fire because today the chief of the Main Staff of the HVO and Mr. Pasalic today issued an order on a cessation to all hostilities, so prevent any deterioration in the situation through peaceful means," that is to say, through negotiations. Now, my question to you, Witness, is this: Did you ever receive an order saying that you should resolve the problems in a different way, any problems that you might have with the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were always given orders to try to resolve the situation peacefully and to resort to negotiations and agreement without making the situation even more tense, and even to give way in certain situations in our relationships with the BH Army. That's what we did. We made several concessions to the BH Army when it came to some MTS that they were asking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, 4D1168. And Arif Pasalic is authorising Esad Ramic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry for taking a few seconds to react to the previous document. My problem is as follows, Witness: We have a request for assistance, artillery. Looking at the document, I may be wrong, but it looks as though this was actually a telex, because there's no signature, and we can see that this document was filed, because we can see a stamp, 23rd of March, 1993. Then Colonel Siljeg took his pen and gave a written explanation to say that there'll be a cessation, et cetera. Hence my question. This is rather strange, as a method, because if Colonel Siljeg receives this fax, that means that he can send a return fax. Why does he decide to write an order to say that nothing is going to be done? And I asked myself whether this was not written later on, because in the heat of the action he received this fax. We might have the hour of receipt if we had the entire document. We could see the top part of the document, but it's not visible here, so it's really difficult when you work with copies. It's best to work with an original document, but we can't ask too much, can we? But supposing that he received this request, because a request for artillery support has to be done straight away, it can't be done three hours or a week later, also because we're dealing with very dramatic news here, as can be seen in the document. And Colonel Siljeg took his pen and wrote by hand. I don't know how he managed to send this handwritten order. In the army, is this something normal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the situation we were in, we asked for reinforcement from the Rama Brigade. Now, this fax from the Rama Brigade was sent on to Mr. Siljeg, and Siljeg responded probably in writing, because we didn't send the fax, but most probably the response was sent in some other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as I understand it, you requested artillery support. And who did you ask this of; of the operative zone, of the North-West Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the North-West Zone of Operations and, more precisely, the Rama Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Who received your fax? Was it Colonel Siljeg or was it the Rama Brigade? Because the operative zone is not the Rama Brigade. Siljeg is the commander of the operative zone, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We sent the request to the Rama Brigade because the situation was such that we were unable to contact Mr. Siljeg, and Rama forwarded our request to Mr. Siljeg because they weren't allowed to use their artillery without Siljeg's approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you made this request to Rama, did you -- or when you make a request, do you make a request by telephone or by fax? How do you go about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll tell you exactly by which means, because the request went from our 1st Battalion which was in the area of Klis and Kostajnica, and I personally was not in the area. I was at Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you know that there had been a request, but you can't say anything as to the details. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, based on your experience, did it happen often that military commanders wrote their orders by hand and it was later retyped, or did they type their orders themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, most times the orders were handwritten, and later on they were typed in various ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have used telexes. Like everybody else, I know how they work. This document we have shows that the commander of the operative zone has received the telex, because we can see the stamp, the incoming stamp. So if he has received the telex, I asked myself, If he is able to receive telexes, why can't he send any? And we have something handwritten. It's not a return telex, but I can see that you can't answer because you were not there and you don't know anything about it. Of course, if Colonel Siljeg had been here, we could have asked this of him. Ms. Alaburic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, I believe we'll have an opportunity to explain what happened with this document later and what is usual in drafting replies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at document 4D1168. It's an authorisation issued by Arif Pasalic to two gentlemen to visit the area of Konjic, Jablanica, and Prozor and contribute to the reduction of tensions between the HVO and the ABiH. Tell me, Witness, does any of these names mean anything to you, and if so, which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Esad Ramic is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was he from Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the commission supposed to calm down the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was one of the members of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Here, the powers of the members of the commission are listed. According to your knowledge, is this an accurate description of their powers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at document 2D1402, 2D1402. Let us see what the significance of the events in Konjic was. These are the conclusions from a session of the HVO of the HZ-HB, dated 24 March 1993. We can read here in the conclusions that: "Calm the current situation in the municipalities of Konjic and Jablanica with all political means ..." Tell me, Witness, can you repeat, because you have said so already, in a way, whether you also received suggestions from the highest political bodies to calm tensions by political means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at document 4D397. This is a document from mid-1992. Let us see whether there was continuity with regard to the way of resolving disputes. This document, dated 20 June 1992, is signed by Milivoj Petkovic, and it says that the Territorial Defence and HVO are constituent parts of the Armed Forces of BiH, and it goes on to say : "Instead of strengthening your mutual bonds in the fight against our common enemy, who is on the threshold of your municipality, you are preparing to use arms against each other." "In the name of Croats and Muslims, I beg you to overcome this situation." You are duty-bound to do that as members of the armed forces of BiH. Tell me, Witness, did you consider yourself as defending Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, sorry for taking some time to ask my questions. You know, Ms. Alaburic is very fast, so by the time I've read the document, the previous document, and I've seen who signed it, I have to ask a question because it is an important one. And if I fail to do it, I don't fulfill my role. On the 24th of March, Mr. Prlic signed a document which shows conclusions of a meeting raising problems or alluding to problems, and it also asks that the presidents of municipalities get together. Under item 7, I can see that Mr. Prlic is asking for the co-presidency of the International Conference, that is, Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen, together with the European Mission and Mr. Izetbegovic, be informed of it all. So any reasonable Judge might infer that Mr. Prlic is perfectly transparent, wants everybody to be informed of what is happening. Based on this document, I'm thinking that if an emissary had been sent from Geneva, somebody neutral tasked with looking at what is happening on the ground, he or she would very quickly have seen who had started -- who was responsible for the situation. You were around there. As far as you can see, if you had somebody coming from outside, from Geneva, or from somewhere else, for that matter, from Berlin or Paris, had come to the area, would that person have been able to know who had done what and why these incidents took place in the Konjic municipality, in the Jablanica municipality, before the 24th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So your answer is, Yes. So this international representative, what would they have highlighted, what salient feature would they have found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But do you think that they could have ascertained the causes and the situation as it really was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if they had closely followed the events on the ground and if they had taken into consideration the reports coming from both sides, that is, the HVO and the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us return to document 4D397. My question is whether you considered that the HVO, that is, the major force of the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was part of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we considered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at a number of documents from March 1993. 4D872, it's a report from the 1st Battalion, Klis, dated 24 March 1993. This battalion belonged to your brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1, it is stated that the forces of the Army fiercely attacked the positions of the HVO, and the military police and the 2nd Battalion were blocked in Konjic. In the city, the flags are being burned and people arrested. Is that an accurate description of the events on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I have already said as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "In the village of Strgovnica, our people were disarmed early this morning, and the HVO cannot transport its wounded to medical care facilities." Is that an accurate description of the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm now skipping two paragraphs, and toward the bottom of the page it reads: "We received unverified information from Konjic that the Suad Alic Brigade had been tasked to defeat us militarily on all positions around Konjic." My question is: Did you have such information about such orders being given to the Suad Alic Brigade, or is this based on an analysis of the events on the ground, or might something else be the source of this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This information is correct, and whoever happened to be at Konjic on that day understood that the action of disarming and defeating the forces of the HVO in this area was in progress because the entire town and the outskirts of the municipality were blocked so that no single member of the HVO could move freely, which Midhat Cerovac, the commander of the 7th Brigade, admitted that because they had disarmed 150 HVO men.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Witness, let's move on to April 1993 and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this is a very detailed document with many detailed items. We learned, for instance, that at the time of the attack, the ABiH had encrypted their radio transmissions, so it's not innocent at all. In Trusina, women and children had been used as human shields, for instance, and there are other examples. But we also find out that the artillery pieces, well, there were T-82 and 102-millimetre mortars, and they had been displaced from the front that was against the Chetniks to be used there. You were then a military man. Was it usual to remove weaponry from the front against the Serbs to use them against those with whom you were fighting the Serbs side by side? So how do you account for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here's how I explain it: According to the order to disarm HVO members, the lines against the Serbs were stable, and this wasn't the first time ABiH members from the front-line -- or moved their weaponry from the front-line, such as mortars, and took them to other places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A minor detail, a political one. The one who drafted this document, Zeljko Mlikota, said this: He said that based on his analysis, there are Muslim politicians who would be in favour of putting an end to the conflict, but they had no influence on the army. The army is not under their influence, it is said. So in the military action of the ABiH, it seems as if it is happening outside the control of some military politicians who seem to be overwhelmed, and that, as a matter of fact, the ABiH intended, rather, to set up a new Muslim authority. So one could believe that within the actual Muslim side, there were differences of opinion between the political part and the military. It's written in here. So what do you think of this? I'm asking for your wise advice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what Zeljko Mlikota meant to say, but it was a well-known fact that there were Muslim politicians who were not in favour of direct conflict, such as Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic. He was probably meant. He tried to reach agreement with the Croatian representatives about not increasing tensions between Croats and Muslims and to preserve peace in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just asked you something about the Muslims. I'm going to have the same questions regarding the Croats. Was it your feeling that at the level of the HZ-HB, there may have been differences between the military structure and the political structure? Were there any differences at all or aren't you aware of the issue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as Konjic is concerned, I can say that all -- everybody from the civilian military structures tried to calm down the situation and avoid a conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that as far as Konjic is concerned, there were no problems between the Croat politicians and military; everybody wanted the end of the conflict. Is that what you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. What I mean to say is that the civilian and military structures wanted to reach an agreement with the Muslim representatives in order to avoid a conflict between the Croats and Muslims, so they tried to normalise relations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's begin with April 1993, and the first document is P1803, P1803. This is a report from the SIS, Rama Brigade, dated the 4th of April, 1993. I'm going to read out a section mentioning Konjic. It says: "In the north-eastern part of Konjic municipality," or "in the eastern part of the municipality leading to Konjic municipality, there were frequent provocations and attempts at attacking villages exclusively populated by Croats." And they are Ivanci, Pajici, and Vratna Gora. "... and because of the fighting and great danger there, the civilian population has moved out. We would like to mention that all these provocations are coming from the villages of Scipe and Kruscica from Konjic municipality." Now, tell us, Witness, this part relating to Konjic, is that a correct report or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, the report is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And was this territory on which your battalion was in charge of the defence or some other unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was territory that our 1st Battalion was in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's repeat that question and answer - it hasn't been recorded - to make life easier. Is this the area for which your battalion was in charge, in defence terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our 1st Battalion was in charge of this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's look at the next document, which is P1810.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. One minor detail in this document. Well, it is a minor detail. Luka Markesic is the author of this document, and this is a situation report he drafted in April, and he reports many facts. But my attention is drawn to the end of the document, in which he mentions incidents with various groups, and he explains that they are forging money, that there is weapon smuggling, looting of apartments and cars and so on, and the author of this report wishes all this to be prosecuted. So you know the events. Can you tell us whether there were groups of people out of control, rogue individuals who would commit various offences, so that the entire army could be blamed if people believed that they were HVO members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably there were individuals, but as far as I know, in my area, where I was, there weren't any such individuals, rogue individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no such group in your zone. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let's look at the next document, which is P1810, 1810. It's a collective report by the Main Staff, dated the 5th of April, and the summary report relates to the 4th of April. And let's look at item 3, the part which relates to Konjic. It says here that from the check-point in Ostrozac, Croats are not being allowed to pass through to Konjic on the pretext that they are preventing people from moving out. Now, is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say that in the village of Prijeslop, a group of BH Army members stormed into the area and looted, damaged property, and expelled the remaining women and children. Is that part correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that part is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, which is 2D774. It's already an exhibit, so we can go through it fairly quickly. This is a report from the 1st Battalion, Klis, which is your brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The report talks about numerous provocations. The village of Gornji Prijeslop is mentioned. Then there's mention about shooting at the barracks and at HVO forces in Seonica, and intensive entrenchment on the part of the Muslim forces. And, finally, it says that threats can be heard ever more frequently by members of the HVO, saying that the Easter in Klis will be a bloody one. Now, Witness, to the best of your knowledge, is what is set out here correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right, let's go on to the next document, which is 2D775.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mention is made in this document of Jusa Hadzajlic, aka Homeini. Apparently, he was someone fueling the conflict, and it's indicated that he could be a KOS member. What is "KOS," in your view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, it is the Counter-Intelligence Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but for whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. KOS was in the former JNA. It was the Counter-Intelligence Service. I can't tell you more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be that this Homeini person was an agent, a Serbian agent, who'd been infiltrated and who would cause conflicts by making speeches, conflicts between the HVO and the ABiH, and would in this way prevent any negotiation? Is that possible, is that something impossible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's look at the next document, 2D775. It's already an exhibit. It is a report from Slavko Puljic in which, among other things, he says that there was an attack on the barracks in Seonica. Tell us, please, Seonica, which army was in Seonica, which forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of the Croatian Defence Council were in the barracks at Seonica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that after the Ivan Sedlo and Duboki Potok barracks, that would be the third perfidiously taken barracks. Is it true that these barracks were seized from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these barracks were seized during the first attack on the 23rd of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 2D76 [as interpreted], the next document, please. 2D776. Once again, Slavko Puljic. It is dated the 9th of April, 1993, and he speaks about further provocations and sniper fire targeting certain Croatian villages. He talks about entrenchment and the looting of empty Croatian villages. Now, to the best of your knowledge, Witness, is this report correct or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go on to the next document, and we'll stay with that document a little longer. It's a very important document, in the view of the Petkovic Defence. It is 2D246. The document, 246, yes -- 2D246. That's right, yes. The document is an exhibit, but let's try and analyse it now, linked to the protocol or minutes that we analysed at length on the meeting between the police and the BH Army on the 23rd of March, which is document 4D454. In point 2 of this document -- or let's identify the document. Who compiled this document, Witness, which unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Enes Kovacevic. That is the unit that was in Jablanica, and the commander was the commander of the Neretva unit from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's see what the BH Army in Jablanica was planning for that day, the 14th of April, 1993. In point 2 of this order, and you've read the document, Witness, previously, because we don't have time to read it from start to finish, anyway, in the last portion of that point it says that they should be on the ready to carry out decisive defence in the direction of Prozor. Now, tell me, Witness, if we were to compare this order with your drawing where you marked the axis of operation, which was on document IC1124, can you tell us what axis this was, which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the direction from Jablanica in the direction of the three villages, Here, Kute and Scipe, so from the western part of Mount Boksevica and part of the front part of Boksevica towards Mrakovo and the other village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's take look at the assignment of the 2nd Battalion set out in point 3. Tell us what the task of the 2nd Battalion was. What was the 2nd Battalion supposed to take control of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion, let me see. That battalion was supposed to take positions towards Ostrozac and Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And what about the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd Company was to deploy the position from Jablanica moving towards Sovici and Doljani, towards Boksevica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I see, towards Boksevica, right. Now let's look at the 3rd Battalion in point 4. It says the task of the 3rd Battalion was to take up positions immediately. And what position was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion was immediately to deploy south of Jablanica towards Mostar at Aleksin Han.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, what was the object of this combat operation, as defined in point 4 of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objective of the combat operation, as defined in point 4, was to block all the access roads going towards Konjic and passing through Jablanica, which meant preventing all possibility of HVO members to come to Konjic as reinforcement and assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You said Aleksin Han was a point south of Jablanica in the direction of Mostar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, if the BH Army, as is stated here, were to take up these positions, take control of these positions, for you, from the direction of Mostar across Jablanica, could any reinforcements and assistance reach you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because that unit would have cut across the communication line from Mostar to Konjic and so prevented any reinforcements from coming in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mostar-Konjic is a relatively long stretch. Now, the positions described in point 4, did they enable the HVO, from the direction of Mostar, reaching Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an obstacle and cut across this communication line, which made it impossible to go from Mostar to Jablanica. At Aleksin Han, a bridge was destroyed and an improvised bridge put up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In point 5, it says that positions towards Risovac should be set up and that the 5th Platoon should be stationed in the village of Doljani, and that it should be prepared to carry out decisive defence until the reinforcements arrive. It says: "Reinforce the position at Obruc by armour-piercing devices and one platoon and set up traffic control." And: "Once the combat operations start, to prevent a breakthrough in the direction of the villages of Sovici and Doljani." So not to allow passage towards Sovici and Doljani. Now, tell us, with this kind of position, would the HVO forces be prevented from arriving in Jablanica? And if your answer is a positive one, then from what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this did prevent arrival through Risovac and Sovicka Vrata and Posusje. It prevented them from arriving in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness, had the BH Army managed to realise its plan, that is to say, to prevent HVO forces from Mostar from reaching the Jablanica area, and from Posusje in the area of Risovac and Sovicka Vrata, what would have happened to the HVO in the area of Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Konjic municipality, the HVO did not have any possibility of sending in reinforcements from whatever direction, which means that the BH Army, by this plan, prevented the arrival of reinforcements and assistance to the Croats in Konjic municipality, and no unit managed to break through and help us in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at item 6. Mention is made again of the direction Jablanica-Plasa, if I read it well, Risovac: "... fully prepared to carry out sabotage against fire positions and fire points in the area between Plasa and Sovicka Vrata, and assist the 4th Battalion in the area of Sovicka Vrata and Borovik." Tell us, along which direction are the places mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are at the Risovac plateau. It's in the direction of Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So it's the communication from Jablanica to Posusje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Under item 7, it is stated that the escort company, following the completed mobilisation, should take positions and be prepared to carry out offensive operations. What is this escort company composed of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The escort company is composed of mortar units, hand-held rocket-throwers, and recoilless guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Under item 8, we can read that: "Soldiers are to be issued two sets of ammunition each ..." Tell us, Witness, based on this information about combat sets of ammunition, what kind of action are the soldiers preparing for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are preparing for combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at item 9. It says that the troops should be supplied with dry meals through the logistics base. When are dry meals provided to troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only for combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's try to sum up. In the first items, the direction of combat activity is defined. You said that it was along the communication to Prozor or Boksevica. Did I understand you correctly? You said that subsequent tasks consist in blocking roads in order to prevent aid coming to the HVO from the directions of Mostar and Posusje; did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we were to look at a map marked IC1123 -- sorry, 1124. That is the map with the positions at number 5 and 7. Witness, do you still have that map?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I would ask for the map to be handed to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now we have the map. We said that point number 7 is according to the attack plan of 23rd of March, 1993. It was document 4D454. And now please show us, Witness, in accordance with this order dated the 14th of April, what is the direction of combat activity of the ABiH brigade at Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The plan of combat activity for the brigade at Jablanica is this direction [indicates], take positions in this direction toward Kute and Scipe --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness has moved away from the microphone. We can't hear him properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let us just precisely describe it, because there is no need to mark it. You didn't say the starting position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We're having a technical problem. Witness, you are speaking too far away from the microphone. Therefore, the interpreters cannot hear you and cannot translate you. It's a bit awkward for you, I'm afraid, but it is necessary that you try to overcome these problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, we said the direction of activity is from where and in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Jablanica toward Prozor and the villages of Here, Kute and Scipe, and the second part towards Boksevica, that is, this part of Boksevica [indicates] toward the Neretva and the lake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do raise the map a little a level to let us see. Now, tell me, the positions that the ABiH should take to prevent help from the south and the west to arrive, that is, from Mostar and Posusje, show them to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of Mostar, this is this part where the -- where there was a bridge which was demolished, Aleksin Han, and a pontoon bridge was constructed instead [indicates], and there was a railroad line from Mostar to Jablanica, so this communication must be cut.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And Posusje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Posusje is in this direction here toward Doljani and Sovici and Sovicka Vrata [indicates]. Here, it was -- or, rather, they had to cut the communication from Posusje, that is, the Risovac plateau.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness, for this. Your Honours, I believe that we can finish for today. We will try to show tomorrow whether the ABiH was able to reach its objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. As you know, we will fortunately be sitting in the morning this week. We'll start tomorrow at 9.00. I believe Ms. Alaburic has about an hour left. I don't have the exact countdown, but it must be close to an hour. Well, our Registrar, quick as a fox, is telling us that you've used two hours and four minutes. You have 56 minutes left, all in all. I was four minutes off. I apologise for that. I wish you all a very pleasant evening, and we'll meet tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 24th day of November, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
